'CAPERNAUM, SAMARIA AND GALILEE, SYRIA AND DAMASCUS, CYPRUS AND ACHAIA, and all the heathen of the district of the Jordan' — NT-ERA APOCALYPTIC TOPONYM CATALOG. The geographic-list is the STRONGEST internal-dating-evidence in 1 Mq for a Christian-era stratum: Capernaum (Mt 11:23 woe-against-Capernaum + the Synoptic Capernaum-Galilean-ministry locus) + Galilee (the standard NT-Galilean-ministry region) + Damascus (Acts 9 Damascus-road Saul-Paul) + Cyprus (Acts 13 Paul-Barnabas mission) + Achaia (Acts 18-19 Pauline-Achaian-mission, including Athens-and-Corinth). The Capernaum-and-Achaia juxtaposition is impossible in pre-Christian-era composition (Capernaum-as-named-significant-locale is a Synoptic-Gospels-era datum; Achaia-as-Roman-province is post-146-BCE but the apocalyptic-pairing-with-Capernaum is NT-era). Per CROSS_REFERENCE_APPENDIX §61 widened-dating: this verse supports the Aksumite-to-Solomonic (4th-14th c.) composition window for the chapter, with the underlying stratum reaching back further.

The geographic-list is the STRONGEST internal-dating-evidence in 1 Mq for a Christian-era stratum: Capernaum (Mt 11:23 woe-against-Capernaum + the Synoptic Capernaum-Galilean-ministry locus) + Galilee (the standard NT-Galilean-ministry region) + Damascus (Acts 9 Damascus-road Saul-Paul) + Cyprus (Acts 13 Paul-Barnabas mission) + Achaia (Acts 18-19 Pauline-Achaian-mission, including Athens-and-Corinth). EXPLICIT LUCIFER-FALL PASSAGE — vv. 12-13 directly cite Isaiah 14:12-14 ('How art thou fallen from heaven, O day-star, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground... I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God'). 1 Mq preserves the standard patristic identification of Isa 14 with the fall of Satan (cf. Tertullian Adversus Marcionem 2.10, Origen De Principiis 1.5.4-5, Augustine City of God 11.15, Cassiodorus Commentary on Psalms). Meqabyan reads Isa 14 as theological-narrative — Lucifer's pride-and-fall as the originating event of the cosmic moral order, the structural pre-condition for the human moral arena that the rest of the trilogy occupies. The chapter is the ESCHATOLOGICAL PIVOT of 1 Mq.
